aggregation.par2_rule: sum full-precision decisive runtimes and 2400 seconds for every unresolved record; round the total to the nearest whole second using round-half-up
aggregation.status_precedence: the result status determines whether a run is decisive; a decisive runtime is included even if collection or cutoff-enforcement latency makes it exceed 1200 seconds

parallel_and_distributed_results.benchmark_identity: benchmark-lists/manifest.csv and the files it names
parallel_and_distributed_results.backend_identity: solver family and version are encoded in result filenames

hardware_environments.earlier_parallel_campaign: one Ubuntu 20.04.4 LTS server with 1 TB RAM and two AMD EPYC 7763 processors, each with 64 physical cores
hardware_environments.distributed_hardware_campaign: Ubuntu 20.04.4 LTS servers with 1 TB RAM and two AMD EPYC 9754 processors per server, each processor with 128 physical cores; p512 uses four servers with 128 configured CPU slots per server
hardware_environments.full_list_p8_ablation_campaign: one server in the distributed-hardware environment

slot_label_semantics.parallel_pN: N configured slots on one server
slot_label_semantics.distributed_sS_pP: S servers with P configured slots per server
slot_label_semantics.manuscript_pN: the complete configured budget of N CPU slots for one configuration-instance run
slot_label_semantics.ariparti_p512: four servers with 128 configured slots each; 504 distributed-tier slots plus an eight-slot isolated allocation containing both the local partition-and-solve branch and the direct complete-instance solver; leader and partitioners share these allocations
slot_label_semantics.other_labels: consult the manuscript and result tables for the comparison scope

parallel_and_distributed_results.cpu_binding: no fixed per-process CPU affinity; slot reservations and worker ceilings define the configured budget
parallel_and_distributed_results.timeout_semantics: the 1200-second application cutoff includes AriParti initialization, partitioning, backend startup, and solving after MPI job startup; the leader checks the cutoff between communication cycles, so completion can exceed the nominal value
parallel_and_distributed_results.campaign_relationship: the main parallel, full-list ablation, and distributed-hardware results are distinct campaigns; earlier parallel p8 and p32 rows are not scaling baselines for distributed p512 rows
parallel_and_distributed_results.resource_sweep_scope: same-campaign full-list QF_NRA results at p32, p64, p128, p256, and p512
parallel_and_distributed_results.distributed_reference_scope: SMTS on QF_LRA and QF_LIA and cvc5-cloud on QF_NRA at p512; the AriParti QF_NIA p512 result has no evaluated distributed reference

cpu_usage.row_semantics: each row contains the CPU value, status, and runtime from one instrumented solver run
cpu_usage.collector_topology: one unbound MPI monitor rank per server; four per-server temporal means are averaged with equal server weight
cpu_usage.sampling: psutil.cpu_percent(interval=0.02, percpu=true) followed by a 0.08-second sleep; nominal 0.1-second cycle plus overhead
cpu_usage.normalization: mean over all logical-CPU percentages visible on a host, multiplied by 512/128 and capped at 100 percent
cpu_usage.measurement_scope: host-wide CPU activity normalized to the configured 128-slot allocation on each of four servers and averaged with equal server weight
cpu_usage.data_scope: each CSV uses the benchmark and row scope defined in distributed/cpu-usage/manifest.csv
cpu_usage.reported_interpretation: end-to-end utilization of each complete configuration

full_list_ablation.public_evidence_level: validated aggregate tables, paired deltas, provenance records, and integrity checks

records: best-effort solver and partitioner version output
